updates.changesSummary: [Distributed Key Manager (DKM)] This update automatically remediates insecure DKM container ACL configurations in AD FS by default. Administrators can opt out of automatic remediation by setting RemediateDkmAcl to 0 . This change helps address an elevation of privilege vulnerability that can occur when the DKM container ACL is overly permissive. For more information about how to manage this change, see CVE-2026-56155: AD FS Distributed Key Manager container ACL hardening . [Secure Boot] This update continues the deployment of updated Secure Boot certificates using the latest high-confidence targeting data to identify eligible devices that are ready to automatically receive the new certificates. Deployment through Windows Update remains ongoing across supported devices.

updates.knownIssuesSummary: USB audio devices might fail to start or produce no sound Symptoms After installing the September 8, 2026, Windows security update (KB5124012), some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices might fail to start or produce audio. Affected devices might experience one or more of the following symptoms: The device displays an error in Device Manager: "This device cannot start (Code 10).” No audio output. Volume controls are unresponsive or remain at zero. Sound settings are unresponsive or unavailable. Some devices might function in standard stereo configurations but fail when using multichannel audio features, including 8-channel or 3D audio modes. Some customers have reported that they're able to restore audio in these cases by switching to 2-channel mode. This issue is limited to USB Audio Class 1.0 devices. Resolution This issue is partially resolved in the out-of-band (OOB) update released on September 14, 2026, (KB5129244) . This OOB update resolves the symptoms experienced on devices using 8-channel or 3D audio modes. Microsoft is working to address the other symptoms and will provide more information when it is available. IT administrators who need an immediate workaround for the symptoms not addressed yet by the OOB update should contact Microsoft Support for Business for assistance.

updates.changesSummary: [Quick machine recovery] New! Quick machine recovery is now supported on Windows Server 2025. During outages, Quick machine recovery helps recover devices from critical boot failures by using Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to find and apply targeted remediations from Windows Update. The feature is disabled by default on Windows Server 2025 editions. Administrators can enable the feature through Group Policy to support streamlined recovery during widespread outages and reduce the need for manual intervention. Recovery depends on an applicable remediation being available. To learn more, see Quick machine recovery . [ReFS security] This update adds auditing and optional policy controls for ReFS volumes on externally attached storage devices. Auditing is enabled by default, while enforcement controls remain disabled by default to give administrators time to evaluate and prepare for future security hardening changes. To learn more, see KB5130741 . [Security] This update adds support for ML-KEM post-quantum key exchange in Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3, helping protect encrypted connections against future quantum-computing threats. [Time and Date] This update updates Windows time-zone data to support permanent daylight-saving time (DST) in British Columbia and Alberta starting in November 2026. This update introduces the new time zone Manitoba Standard Time "(UTC-5:00) Manitoba". [Security] This update upgrades the version of cURL included with Windows to version 8.21.0. [Networking] This update improves the NetUseAdd function, helping it establish SMB network connections successfully during NULL session attempts. [Authentication] This update improves Netlogon secure channel connections, helping member servers connect successfully to domain controllers that were set up before Windows Server 2025. [Emoji] This update improves security for emoji search in the Expressive Input Panel by updating the libraries used by EmojiSearchData. [Hyper-V] This update improves the reliability of Intel Trusted Domain Extensions (TDX) confidential virtual machines in Hyper-V reliability issues affecting TDX operation. [Distributed Key Manager (DKM)] This update automatically remediates insecure DKM container ACL configurations in AD FS by default. Administrators can opt out of automatic remediation by setting RemediateDkmAcl to 0 . This change helps address an elevation of privilege vulnerability that can occur when the DKM container ACL is overly permissive. For more information about how to manage this change, see CVE-2026-56155: AD FS Distributed Key Manager container ACL hardening . Deployment through Windows Update remains ongoing across supported devices.

After sign-in, Explorer.exe might fail to start or repeatedly crash, causing a black screen. When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed. In some cases, subsequent connection attempts could display the error, "The specified port is already in use." [Storage Spaces] This update fixes an issue that affects tiered Storage Spaces Direct virtual disks. Some virtual disks might fail to come online after installing certain security updates, making dependent clustered workloads unavailable. [Printing] This update resolves an issue where printing could fail in some applications and on devices using RAW or Generic Text Only printer drivers after installing the August 2026 security update. [Gaming] This update fixes an issue that could cause mouse input to stutter in some games. [Windows Hello] This update fixes an issue where fingerprint sign-in might not work after a cold boot on some devices.
updates.knownIssuesSummary: Remote Desktop connections might fail for non-admin users with error 0xC000000D Symptoms After installing the September 2026 non-security preview update KB5124010 , or later updates, non-admin users might be unable to establish Remote Desktop connections to remote devices that have Administrator protection enabled. Attempts to connect might fail with error 0xC000000D and display the message, “The token that was passed to the function is invalid.” This issue primarily affects enterprise-managed remote devices used as Remote Desktop hosts with Administrator protection enabled, regardless of how the feature was enabled . Note: If your organization uses Windows security baselines , published through the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit , Administrator protection is enabled by default in Windows 11, version 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 security baselines, unless your organization has configured the policy differently. Resolution IT administrators can mitigate this issue on devices affected by the Remote Desktop connection failure by using their existing policy management method to temporarily turn off Administrator protection. Reset the User Account Control Type Of Admin Approval Mode policy in Microsoft Intune or Group Policy. For more information, see Administrator protection on Windows 11 . Next steps: Microsoft is working to address this issue in a future Windows update and will provide more information when it is available.
